name: SessionBench + Resident-Slot SLA (benchmark-first, Wafer-motion)
one_line: Publish an open sessions-per-GPU-at-SLO benchmark, ship the pinned-RAM residency connector + idle-hint pinning protocol that moved the voice knee 1.5x (one seed, L40S), and sell warm session-slots per slot-hour to voice/agent platforms via Wafer-style engagements and dedicated endpoints.
evidence_grade_reason: The benchmark leg is real (287,015 archived in-engine turns, recomputed) but every headline is single-seed, synthetic-trace, one 46 GB GPU, a 7B fp16 model, and vLLM 0.9.2 with unarchived server metrics. The runtime leg's core claim (1.5x knee move) is measured once with an 8.1 ms full-load margin, fails the brief's own 6-of-7-bucket criterion (recomputed from events.jsonl: 311.8/306.5/303.9 ms), fails at N=400, and its policy delta over the plain connector is 44.6 ms at one SLO (1.0x ratio at 350-400 ms). The restore-vs-re-prefill physics behind the RAM tier is contradicted across the dexa repo under concurrency (04-conflicts.md §1), and the slot-SLA layer, every 2026 OSS baseline, the H100 point, real traffic, and customer-class models are unmeasured. That is 'measured but bounded/contradicted' = C; a same-version, 3-seed, two-GPU run with archived correctness would lift it to B.
build_cost_weeks_to_proof: 8-10 weeks to a credible public benchmark on synthetic traces (3 seeds, L40S + H100, all arms on the same vLLM 0.28 incl. OffloadingConnector / LMCache 0.5.4 / HiCache, archived server metrics and restore-correctness, SLO curve), assuming 2 engineers, Modal access, ~250 GPU-h (~$600-900 at Modal L40S $1.95/hr, H100 $3.95/hr), and the vLLM 0.9.2->0.28 connector port landing in <=2 weeks (the API is 'experimental'; dexa needed live probes for 0.24). 12-16 weeks for the same benchmark on partner transcripts, since the converter is partner-gated. The draft's 6 weeks assumed ~120 GPU-h (undercounted ~2x), a one-week port bundled with free-at-turn-end and async loads, and a design partner with converted traces by Week 5.

attacks.attack: The runtime's measured advantage is an SLO-threshold artifact. At 300 ms, arm D passes N=300 (291.9 ms full-load) and the plain VoiceKVConnector fails (336.8 ms); at any SLO of 350-400 ms both hold N=300 and the pinning policy's entire measured contribution is a 44.6 ms p95 shift with ~0 change at p50. Twilio's published LLM-TTFT budget is 375 ms target / 750 ms max, so a buyer using industry budgets would see the 'policy layer' as a free feature and the real win as the contiguous transfer path (which is a connector, not a policy).
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Report N* for A, B-voice and D as a curve over SLO in {200, 300, 400, 500 ms} at 3 seeds on L40S; if D = B-voice at >=3 of 4 thresholds the policy leg is not a product, only the connector and harness are.

attacks.attack: The draft's own pre-registered pass criterion ('full-load p95 <= 300 ms in >= 6 of 7 five-minute buckets') is failed by the only existing measurement: arm D N=300 has 3 of 7 buckets above 300 ms (311.8, 306.5, 303.9 ms, recomputed from events.jsonl). The draft presents arm D as the runtime that 'wins' SessionBench while defining a benchmark that, run today, would report 'no runtime passes at N=300 on L40S'.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Seeds 2-3 for arms A/B-voice/D at N in {250,300,350} with pin budget 10 and 16 GB; proceed only if the 3-seed median clears 6/7 at N>=280.

attacks.attack: Engine-version confound plus OSS catch-up. Every baseline was vLLM 0.9.2 + LMCache 0.3.2 in two untuned configs (Aug 2026 runs on a year-old engine). vLLM 0.28's native OffloadingConnector (DMA, lru/arc; IBM blog claims 2-22x TTFT on Llama-8B/H100), LMCache 0.5.4, SGLang HiCache and Dynamo KVBM have never been run on this harness. Worse, the draft's Week-2 plan runs arm D on 0.9.2 (port is Week 3) against OSS baselines on 0.28, so any published headline would be mixed-version.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Port first; run every arm on one vLLM version (0.28) with OffloadingConnector and LMCache 0.5.4 tuned per their docs (layerwise on, chunk-size sweep); kill the runtime leg if any OSS stack holds N=300 <= 300 ms out of the box.

attacks.attack: A bigger-HBM GPU or FP8 KV erases the wall. 04-conflicts.md §5 arithmetic: an 80 GB GPU with the same 7B weights leaves ~60 GB of KV pool, which fits the ~42 GB N=300 working set and moves the arm-A cliff to ~N 400-450; FP8 KV halves bytes and moves the baseline wall too. Both repos call this the #1 threat and neither measured it. A 'well-configured baseline' is simply an H100.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Arm A and D at N=300/400/500 on H100-80GB with FP8 KV on/off; kill if A's knee >= 2x L40S and D < 1.2x on H100.

attacks.attack: The connector cannot serve the customers' models. VoiceKVConnector is TP=1 only, fp16/bf16 only (dtype_size hardcoded 2), non-MLA paged layout, prompt-KV only, synchronous loads inside the scheduler step, pinned to vLLM 0.9.2's batched CachedRequestData shape. Buyer 1 runs Gemma 4 31B (62 GB fp16 weights do not fit an L40S), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE, and MLA models (GLM/Kimi/DeepSeek); a 31B model on H100 at TP=1 leaves ~15 GB of KV pool. Nothing measured transfers to a 26-35B deployment.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: One 26-35B model with fp8 weights on H100 at TP=1 through the ported connector, arms A and D at N sweep; MLA and TP>1 support are new code with unknown cost.

attacks.attack: Correctness and internal thrash are unarchived. evals/modal_kv_correctness.py exists but its output was never committed and FINDINGS §4 implies text divergence was observed; missing-entry loads would silently fill garbage KV. Separately, code reading shows a store evicts the slab entry it matched, so sessions sharing a customer system prompt (5 prompts across 300 sessions) evict each other's slab entries every turn -- the recorded 35-52% hit rates (themselves unarchived) may reflect this bug, and a retention SLA built on it would silently miss.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Archive the bitwise round-trip and forced-evict probe; re-key entries per session; scrape server hit/restore counters into events.jsonl; run the --shared-prompt confound and compare hit rate before/after the fix.

attacks.attack: Arm D's predictor knows the answer. The idle hint is max_tokens x 308 ms TTS - generation at 45 tok/s + the trace's own median gap (400 ms), median utterance (2,500 ms) and STT delay -- constants of the generating distribution. Barge-ins (10%) and spurious VAD (5%) are ignored. Real-call idle fraction is unmeasured (Phase 0 is synthetic and computed at the wrong KV geometry and decode rate), speech-to-speech models may collapse the idle window entirely, and the synthetic 75-token replies (~23 s of TTS) drive the 95% idle figure.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Partner-transcript converter; Phase 0 rerun at 57,344 B/token and 45 tok/s; arm D with a hint fitted on held-out sessions and an ablation with barge-in/spurious-VAD stripped; kill if real idle < 40% or held-out D gain < 50% of in-sample.

attacks.attack: The retention SLA's honoring mechanism at scale is the arm that fails. Pinning holds HBM under a 10 GB budget (~70 sessions); every retained session beyond the budget is a RAM-tier restore, i.e. the B-voice configuration that fails the 300 ms gate at N=300 (336.8 ms full-load) and puts ~17 ms of restore on the p95 path (p50 100 ms under load vs a 7 ms docstring estimate isolated). Free-at-turn-end, the mechanism that would bound HBM so more slots could be pinned, was described in the PRD and never built. The SLA layer is therefore a design on top of a fallback that misses the SLO.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Honor-rate experiment: % of retained sessions warm at return under a pin budget with adversarial load, with server-side hit rate archived; plus the free-at-turn-end run measuring HBM pool occupancy at N=300/400.

attacks.attack: The agent leg has no in-engine evidence and the physics is contradicted. All production-engine restore evidence stops at 16k (vLLM crashed >=32k in the dexa harness); the 64k/28.9x and 4.9-hr NVMe break-even are HF-tensor numbers; dexa's own connector lost to vLLM re-prefill at 8k (0.37x) and under 16-24-way concurrency (disk tier). TraceLab's 126k-token prefixes are ~7 GB each at 7B fp16, so 300 resident agent sessions need ~2 TB of pinned RAM; RAM-tier aggregate bandwidth at that scale under concurrency is unmeasured anywhere.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: The crossover-surface experiment in 04-conflicts.md §1: one model, one GPU, contexts {4k..64k} x concurrency {1,8,32,128} x {re-prefill, LMCache layerwise, contiguous pinned-RAM connector with async load, NVMe}; kill the agent leg if RAM-tier p99 TTFT improvement at 64k/16-way < 2x.

attacks.attack: The product interface is a bet on unstable APIs. vLLM's KVConnector V1 docstring still says 'experimental and subject to change'; the retain protocol depends on kv_transfer_params passthrough and request_finished delayed-free semantics that exist in 0.9.2 and must be re-verified in 0.28 (dexa needed live probes to discover 0.24's 3-arg constructor); SGLang RFC #27574 is open with only a draft Mooncake POC; Dynamo's TTL retention semantics are documented only in a blog. Two of the three engine paths do not exist yet.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Measure the 0.9.2 -> 0.28 port in engineer-weeks (kill > 2) and confirm delayed-free + kv_transfer_params semantics survive; track RFC #27574 status.

attacks.attack: The 6-week plan slips on three known items: the ~120 GPU-h budget undercounts Week 2 (5 arms x 2 GPUs x 3 seeds x ~4 N points at ~55 min each is ~120 runs on its own); Week 3 bundles the experimental-API port, free-at-turn-end and async loads into one week; Week 5 needs a design partner with converted transcripts although discovery starts Week 1 and the converter is partner-gated. Realistic: 9-12 weeks to the synthetic-trace publication, 12-16 with partner traces.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Not a measurement; re-sequence (port first, publish on synthetic traces, partner report in Weeks 8-12) and budget ~250 GPU-h.

attacks.attack: Hosted-endpoint comparisons produce a different quantity. Running Fireworks, Wafer, LiveKit Inference or Tensormesh through the same client yields a knee-at-RPM curve with unknown GPU count behind it, not sessions/GPU; a leaderboard that mixes the two invites the 'apples and oranges' rebuttal Wafer's own posts (knee-at-RPS with a stated TTFT bound) would make.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Keep two tracks with different metrics; only self-hosted stacks with a known GPU count enter the sessions/GPU table.

attacks.attack: Reproducibility is weaker than 'pre-registered gates' suggests: every Modal manifest records git_sha 'unknown' and no connector field (arm B-LMCache vs B-VoiceKV is distinguished by directory name and prose); whether --max-num-seqs 256 applied to the arm A sweep is unrecorded; only 5 distinct system prompts (the PRD's own §9 says this flatters arm A); the arm C archive's server died at minute 41 with 37% of turns missing a TTFT.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Add connector/flags/git-sha provenance to manifests and rerun arm A with recorded flags before publishing any baseline number.

attacks.attack: H100 physics in the brief is derived, not measured: PCIe Gen5 128 GB/s is the H100 spec sheet, H100 prefill tok/s for these models is unmeasured, and the '~60 GB pool / cliff ~N 400-450' is arithmetic on the L40S OVERLOAD.md numbers.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: The H100 arm A/D point plus evals/modal_lmcache_restore.py rerun on H100 to feed measured prefill/restore into stateful_cost_model.py.

missing_founder_decisions: The SLO itself: the draft adopted the PRD's 300 ms p95 TTFT as the benchmark's defining threshold; Twilio budgets 375 ms target / 750 ms max for LLM TTFT and LiveKit reports 192 ms. The threshold determines whether the pinning policy has any measured edge (at 350-400 ms, D and B-voice tie).

The pass criterion and aggregation window: the draft chose '>= 6 of 7 five-minute buckets <= 300 ms' (which existing data fails) and the full-load window (minutes 5-40) rather than whole-run; each choice moves arm D between pass and fail.
The target ratio (1.4x) chosen below the voice PRD's own 2x proceed line and inside the README's '<2x kill' band.
Selling upstream to platforms/providers rather than downstream to end builders (the thesis assumes it; §11 lists it but the customer section is written as if decided).
GTM as Wafer-motion engagements + dedicated endpoints rather than software/BYOC (Tensormesh Operator model) or OSS harness + paid certification.
Not forking vLLM/SGLang (carrying the PRD's constraint forward), which forecloses the scheduler-native prefetch the repo calls the strongest untested form of the thesis.
Engine neutrality and publicly scoring OSS stacks (OffloadingConnector, LMCache, HiCache, KVBM) beside K's runtime -- a choice that may hand competitors the result.
The v0 rig: Qwen2.5-7B fp16 on L40S/H100, not the 26-35B / A3B MoE / MLA models platforms actually run.
The pricing unit: slot-hour by tier, rather than per-line/month (Vapi, Retell), cached-token retention with TTL (DeepInfra, Gemini), or % of estimated savings (Tensormesh).
Requiring both a 46 GB and an 80 GB GPU in the proof (two-GPU criterion) rather than one class.
Trace source: synthetic + partner transcripts, rather than public traces (Mooncake traces per docs/BENCHMARK_PLAN.md, TraceLab) for the first publication.
Bundling three products (benchmark, runtime, SLA/billing) into one company rather than sequencing or choosing one.
Tenant isolation of KV (single-tenant vs shared slots; tenant-namespaced keys) and guarantee-with-credits vs best-effort-with-metrics.
Whether hosted endpoints (Fireworks, Wafer, LiveKit Inference, Tensormesh) appear on the leaderboard at all, given they yield knee-at-RPM not sessions/GPU.
Whether SessionBench checks output quality/correctness (the harness measures serving behavior only; restore correctness is unarchived).
strongest_version: K's defensible core is a harness that already produced 287,015 archived in-engine multi-turn turns and caught the depth-triggered collapse that a 10-minute load test would miss; no engine, provider or voice platform in the research files publishes sessions-per-GPU at a p95-TTFT SLO, and the platforms that would buy it already sell concurrency per line. The strongest honest form leads with that benchmark as a Wafer-style engagement ('we measured your cliff on your traces and your GPU'), publishes an SLO curve rather than a single 300 ms number, and treats the residency runtime as the current best-known configuration that moved one measured knee 1.5x -- a result to be replicated at 3 seeds on the same engine version as OffloadingConnector and LMCache 0.5.4 before it is sold. The slot-hour SLA becomes a product only after the honor-rate and H100 gates pass; until then it is a pricing sheet priced off list L40S rates ($0.0026-0.0075 per slot-hour at N*=300) that customers can compare against Managed Agents' $0.08/session-hour and DeepInfra's TTL retention multipliers. If the 2026 OSS stacks hold N=300 out of the box, K still owns the standard, the certification and the retention policy; if an H100 dissolves the L40S wall, K still owns the measurement that proved it. The company is worth starting on the benchmark and the engagement motion; the runtime and the SLA are hypotheses with pre-registered kill gates and roughly 8-10 weeks to a credible public proof.

Added to §1 that adjacent public agent-trace benchmarks exist (vLLM/Mooncake, llm-d, VAST/Backend.AI) while the exact sessions-per-GPU-at-SLO metric remains unpublished.

Stated explicitly in §4 that the existing arm-D measurement fails the brief's own >=6-of-7-bucket criterion (3 of 7 buckets above 300 ms: 311.8/306.5/303.9, recomputed from events.jsonl) and that the policy delta over the plain connector is 44.6 ms p95 / ~0 p50 with a 1.0x ratio at 350-400 ms SLO; made the metric an SLO curve.

Corrected the §6 attribution of the 10/10-hook conformance result to DexaConnector on vLLM 0.24.0 (not VoiceKV, which is pinned to 0.9.2); added the model caveats to cross-instance resume (OPT-125m/Qwen3-0.6B, A10G) and to the fp8 result (HF-level, one passage, 48 tokens) and removed 'fp8 storage' as a blob-format feature.
Corrected the connector line numbers (179-183, 338-367, 369-379, 429-447; run.py:86-92) after verifying in the repo.

Rewrote the §5 table: connector marked as vLLM 0.9.2 with the 0.28 port as new work and its limits listed (TP=1, fp16/bf16, non-MLA, prompt-KV only, synchronous loads); free-at-turn-end listed as never built; SLA meter reuse reduced to key hashing + daily rollups; dexa edge/ removed as an affinity option (single-backend scaffold, never deployed); tier table marked modeled/advisory.
